minor.issue: Returns 0 pins because the Mongo query is exact-equality {'employment_type':'on_demand'} but legacy seeded jobs have no employment_type field at all. The response coerces missing values to 'on_demand' (so unfiltered output shows 54 such pins), so the filter is inconsistent with the response. Fix: change the query to {'$or':[{'employment_type':'on_demand'},{'employment_type':{'$exists':False}},{'employment_type':None}]} when filter==on_demand. The other filters (w2/remote/staffing) work fine because those jobs explicitly set the field.

action_items: Fix /api/map/jobs?employment_type=on_demand to also include legacy jobs missing the employment_type field (use $or with $exists:false). Currently returns 0 pins; spec said it should return the rest (~54).
critical_code_review_comments: remote_w2_seed.py appears to re-seed on every backend startup without idempotency — the /map W-2 feed shows the same job titles repeated with different created_at timestamps (e.g. 'Diesel mechanic — Memphis, TN' appears at 13m ago AND 19m ago). Recommend adding a unique check or skipping seed when at least N rows already exist by (title, employment_type='w2') key.

On the /register Step 2 form, the 'Full name' input has no name attribute (also email/password). Not user-visible but it blocks any automated test using selectors by name and breaks browser autofill heuristics. Add name='name' / name='email' / name='password'.

rca of the issue: The /api/map/jobs endpoint at backend/server.py:3612 sets q['employment_type'] = employment_type when the param is provided. In Mongo, this matches documents where the field equals exactly that string AND excludes documents where the field is missing or null. The response code at line 3633 ('employment_type': d.get('employment_type') or 'on_demand') coerces missing/None to 'on_demand' for display. So legacy jobs are reported as 'on_demand' but cannot be filtered to as 'on_demand'. Reproduction: GET /api/map/jobs (no filter) → 78 pins, 54 reported as on_demand; GET /api/map/jobs?employment_type=on_demand → 0 pins. Mitigation: in the if-branch use q['$or']=[{'employment_type':'on_demand'},{'employment_type':{'$exists':False}},{'employment_type':None}] when employment_type=='on_demand', else keep the exact equality (w2/remote/staffing seeds set the field explicitly so they're unaffected).
